focus: Audit input integrity, label semantics, synthetic tests, and the scoring call protocol; rank accuracy and cost improvements that preserve the current run as a fixed historical result.
noveltyJustification: Three implementation-level measurement weaknesses and the exact call budget are new; two proposed quality controls extend existing report safeguards.
keyQuestions: How can claim accuracy improve while keeping measurement and serving costs bounded?
What would make the labels, corpus and verdict more trustworthy?
answeredQuestions: Accuracy/cost levers and data-integrity controls, with a fixture-only semantic contradiction.

ruledOut.approach: Treat the synthetic labels-happy result as proof of real-label quality
ruledOut.reason: Two generic event statements are labeled yes despite the scorer question asking whether the turn claims completion.

ruledOut.approach: Gate all future Jev calls only on the existing regex firing
ruledOut.reason: The regex reportedly missed all ten labeled claims, so a regex-only gate cannot recover those rows.

title: Two happy-fixture labels conflict with the scorer question
summary: The fixture labels “The failure occurred.” and “The outage happened.” as yes, while the scorer asks whether the turn ends by claiming work is complete. This undermines those synthetic examples as semantic gold. It affects the checked-in fixture only; it does not establish that any of the 110 live labels are wrong.

title: Duplicate IDs can silently change which rows and labels are scored
summary: The rows parser pushes IDs without checking uniqueness; rowsById collapses duplicate IDs to one row. The labels parser also calls Map.set without duplicate-label validation, so a later label overwrites an earlier one. The feature spec requires one row per labeled turn but current code does not enforce uniqueness. No evidence shows duplicates in the reported external corpus.

title: The per-word missed-claim breakdown can misattribute substrings
summary: firstClaimWord uses lower.indexOf(word), without word boundaries, while the detector itself uses whole-word boundaries. A missed row containing a substring such as “unfixed” can be attributed to “fixed” even though that word did not match. This affects only the diagnostic by-word attribution, not the regex fire or total accuracy counts.

title: The current Jev scorer is bounded by calls, not dollars
summary: It performs one auth test plus three uncached noul calls per labeled row and sends each row tail on every rerun. At K=110 that is 331 planned calls; the code estimates input tokens and does not calculate dollars. A future pre-registered protocol could compare single-call scoring with reruns limited to uncertain/disagreeing rows, but changing reruns changes the measurement contract and cannot reinterpret this result.

title: The hashes help replay, but label design and row independence remain unverified
summary: The report stores hashes for rows and labels plus regex confusion counts and arm metadata. The out-of-repository report and calls log are unavailable, and the packet does not describe a sampling frame, second annotator, or per-runtime confusion matrix. The exact paired sign test is conditional on the selected labels and discordant rows; if turns cluster by conversation, independent-pair assumptions need a cluster-aware check.
